market_story: CC committed block: a synchronised ERCOT combined cycle does not offer its first above-min-load MW at its average burn. The real fleet anchors its RT curve at ~$10/MWh at 2024 gas and ~$18 at 2025 gas (measured SCED TPO-Price1 p50, corroborated within ~$1 by the units' own declared Min-Gen-Cost at 70-82 % coverage) — a level BELOW its own fuel cost, because the alternative for an already-committed unit is decommitment, so the offer that matters is its avoidable cost net of the start it would re-pay, not its average heat rate. That is the same economics coal's take-or-pay min-load block has, which ERCOT-137 put on a measured basis; gas had no such mechanism, so the model priced 28 % of its CC capability ~$7.4/MWh dearer than the fleet does in every measured subset and coal correctly won a merit order it should have lost. With the block on its measured level, coal gives back 3.0-3.8 TWh/yr and CC takes 4.5-5.2 — and because the block is inframarginal in every scarcity hour, none of the scarcity tail moves. What the arm does NOT fix, and does not pretend to: the model's curve is too flat at the TOP (coal's p90 runs $9.6-15.5/MWh under measured), which is why the mean price falls further as the crossing band is corrected. That is the near-tail lane, not this one.
